scope: Existing text-only character-arc entries paired only where the exact reviewed photograph supports the scene. This is deliberately four candidates, not twelve: the rest of the tempting catalog matches either already illustrate their own episode or fail the visible-action test.
selectionPolicy: A photograph must support the entry's central event or its concrete aftermath. Same species alone is insufficient. A reallocation candidate is not an additional binding: the editor must retain either the existing binding or the rescue binding.

original.title: Tomorrow, definitely
original.body: She turned toward me and I forgot the beautiful approach I had rehearsed. Took one step forward. Took it back. She caught a fly without looking away. I have decided to approach tomorrow.

inspection.visibleFacts: Two green praying mantises are closely coupled upright on a green plant.

candidates.proposedBody:
She turned toward me and I forgot the beautiful approach I had rehearsed. Took one step forward. Took it back. She caught a fly without looking away.

Then I took another step. She did not leave. The rehearsed part remained unavailable, but the afternoon became considerably more crowded.
candidates.visibleFit: The original ending puts the approach off-frame in the future, while the reviewed photograph makes the already-close encounter central. This minimal ending adjustment lets the visible pair be the payoff without claiming a detail the frame cannot show.
candidates.imageAvailability: unused by the current character arcs

original.title: The wrong side showed
original.body:
He approached on my left while I was watching another cuttlefish on my right. My skin changed before I had decided which encounter I was having.

I turned toward him. He hesitated. I softened the pattern, then made it stronger, then swam forward much too abruptly.

He moved with me. We traveled beside each other without touching. It was easier once there was a direction to go.

inspection.reviewMethod: Direct image review of the catalog image URL
inspection.visibleFacts: Two patterned cuttlefish rest close together on pale rubble, angled toward one another; a dark branching structure crosses the foreground.

candidates.visibleFit: This is not a species portrait. The two-animal composition supports the hesitant, close-quarters courtship beat and the final side-by-side movement. The third cuttlefish remains off-frame rather than falsely asserted visible.
candidates.identityNote: The catalog's stock label is Cuthbert Chromatic, not a canon arc. It must not be presented as Iris and a named recurring Cuthbert without a separate canon decision.
candidates.imageAvailability: unused by the current character arcs

original.title: The empty place underneath
original.body:
The crab left while I was feeding. I noticed when I moved and nothing adjusted beneath me.

I stopped, which was silly. It had spent our entire acquaintance demonstrating that stopping would not persuade it to do anything.

A few steps later it caught up and tucked itself back underneath. I continued at my previous pace. Possibly a little slower where the ground was uneven.

inspection.reviewMethod: Direct image review of the catalog image URL
inspection.visibleFacts: A pale sea pig stands on sediment with a small pink crab directly beneath its body.

candidates.visibleFit: The reviewed frame directly supplies the emotional fact of the rescue: the returning crab has resumed shelter beneath Percy. It is substantially more specific to this entry than a generic sea-pig image would be.

reallocation.originalBoundBody:
A small crab had tucked itself beneath me. I could feel the difference when it moved. At first I stopped every time, waiting for it to get off.

It stayed through three stops and one fairly pointed change of direction.

I resumed eating. The crab drew its legs closer underneath me and settled against my belly.
reallocation.decision: Choose one only. The existing bound episode introduces the relationship; this rescue gives its later return a stronger emotional consequence.

original.title: What holds me up
original.body:
I lifted until my tentacles lost the bottom. For a moment there was no solid thing touching me. Only water against the thin edges of my body and the weight of the meal inside.

I spread myself farther. The water held me. It had been doing that all along, but usually I was too busy trying to get somewhere to feel how much of me it carried.

Then the meal shifted. I folded, sank, and touched down mouth first. I can be moved by an experience and still land badly.

media.creator: NOAA Okeanos Explorer; color adjustment by Togabi

inspection.reviewMethod: Direct image review of the catalog image URL
inspection.visibleFacts: A translucent red swimming sea cucumber is suspended above a pale seafloor. Its looped gut is conspicuous through the body and thin membrane edges are spread into the water.

candidates.visibleFit: The photograph visibly makes water support, spread body edges, and the awkwardly carried meal the scene. It is a precise visual counterpart to this entry, not merely a specimen photograph.

reallocation.originalBoundBody: Someone said I should leave a little to the imagination. I tried turning sideways. My intestine came with me.
reallocation.decision: Choose one only. The existing micro-post is funny but functions as a caption for the visible gut. This rescue is a fuller scene whose stated lift and visible anatomy meet in the same frame.

excludedAfterInspection.title: The tail dissents
excludedAfterInspection.reason: The reviewed chameleon is on a branch with its tail curled, but the photograph does not show the tail still gripping a previous branch. It is an avatar, not an honest scene match.

excludedAfterInspection.title: Useful resemblance
excludedAfterInspection.reason: The reviewed leaf-tailed gecko has a remarkable leaf-shaped body on a branch, but no bird or leaf-turning action is visible. The visual premise alone is not enough.

excludedAfterInspection.title: He recognized the mouth
excludedAfterInspection.reason: The reviewed ribbon eel emerges with its mouth open, but no second eel or neighboring opening is visible. It cannot carry the reconciliation scene.

excludedAfterInspection.title: A passenger with opinions
excludedAfterInspection.reason: The reviewed turtle image shows a turtle swimming above reef with small fish, not a visible remora attachment. It would be a generic turtle substitution.
